request: Quick fun fact video about octopus hearts for TikTok.
intent: Social media viewers want a surprising fact they can repeat.
goal: The viewer remembers three hearts, what each does, and that the third stops when swimming.
arc: Three hearts appear, two at the gills and one for the body, then the third one stops.

events.text: Two pump blood through the gills. The third pumps it to the rest of the body.
events.knows: Two for the gills, one for the body.
events.look: the two gill hearts, then the third heart

events.text: And when it swims, that third heart stops. Which is why octopuses would rather crawl.
events.knows: The body heart stops while swimming.

measure.derived: Derived once from the request, intent and audience; thresholds not named here take the defaults in bench/lib/settings.ts. Read sizes scale with how wide the frame looks: a classroom or meeting screen from the back looks narrower than a phone at arm's length, a laptop at a desk wider. A hold listed as still is one the plan asks to wait without motion.

quiz.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
What do two of the hearts do?
What happens to the third heart when it swims?

quiz.a: The third one, the one that pumps blood to the rest of the body.

quiz.q: Which hearts were lit first in the second scene?
Which heart was lit after the gill hearts?
quiz.a: The third one, for the body.

quiz.q: Which heart stopped: the pair or the single one?
